rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers that receive City of Boston Department of Neighborhood Development funding or land, or that have income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, cannot use a blanket ban on arrests or convictions to deny housing; they must consider applicants case-by-case and may not consider arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old.
rules.key_value: 5-year conviction lookback; no blanket criminal history denials
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding/land or with BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units
rules.exemptions: Exemption does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to safety of others
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span:
The Developer/Agent (Agent) agrees to not consider any of the following categories when 
determining housing eligibility and or considering eviction: 
 
a) Arrests that did not result in conviction. This includes dismissed charges, diversion 
programs, and similar non-convictions.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the housing provider receives DND funding/land or has BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units

rules.conflict_note: This is a policy tied to DND funding/BPDA units rather than a generally applicable ordinance covering all multifamily buildings citywide.
